notes: §1985:VIII.4.2.4 GR5: 'Following the successful execution of a CLOSE statement, the record area associated with file-name-1 is no longer available. The unsuccessful execution of such a CLOSE statement leaves the availability of the record area undefined.' The rule withdraws the area from a conforming program and defines nothing about referencing it, so the implementation obligation is only that CLOSE succeed or fail as the other rules say: FileRegistry.CloseByFormat closes the connector (42 when not open), and the record is a typed field of the emitted class whose content survives, the determination documented at docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-24; FileControlBinder.LinkSameRecordArea keeps one storage area for a SAME RECORD AREA group. Probes at --std 85 (classes a, d, e): a RELATIVE DYNAMIC file whose record holds an OCCURS 1 TO 8 DEPENDING ON table, in SAME RECORD AREA with a sequential file: after CLOSE of the relative file the still-open sequential file's record shows the shared bytes and writes; READ after reopen gives [05QQQQQ]; after a successful CLOSE the area keeps [05QQQQQ] (00), after a failed CLOSE (42) likewise, a reference-modified MOVE into the closed area runs without fault, and a reopen and READ restore the record (00). Classes b, c, f do not apply (no syntax of its own). The witness reads, saves the record to Working-Storage before the CLOSE, and displays the saved copy.

next.reason: 1985: "Following the successful execution of a CLOSE statement, the record area associated with file-name-1 is no longer available."; 2023: "the record area is available to the runtime element if any of the file connectors referenced by the other file-names in that SAME RECORD AREA clause are open". 2023 keeps the rule (unavailable after success, undefined after failure) but adds a case: the area stays available while another file in the same SAME RECORD AREA clause is open.
